title: Registry: registry-db datastore VRRP failover (.119 cutover + fence/re-seed)
description: Runs `nexus failover-test cluster registry --direction registry-db --yes`. Stops keepalived on the VIP .119-holding datastore primary; notify_master promotes PG (pg_ctl promote) + re-masters Redis; the adapter then fences + pg_basebackup re-seeds the OLD primary as a fresh streaming standby (nexus-registry-reseed.sh, guarded so it can never wipe a live primary), and restarts keepalived (whose notify_backup demote.sh re-points the old Redis to the new master). 0.L.4.1 fencing hardening: the NEXUS-REGISTRY-HBA block is now on BOTH nodes so the promoted node admits the Harbor DB user -> no split-brain, Harbor stays served. Was code-verified-but-DR-deferred before this hardening.

prerequisites.notes: registry-pg-1/2 are the datastore pair (VIP registry-db.nexus.lab .119, PG :5432 + co-located Redis :6379). The Harbor app nodes (registry-1/2) are RR-DNS and NOT required for the drill — power them on only to observe Harbor end-to-end. MinIO is not required for the catalog-DB path.

observe.what: VIP .119 moves registry-pg-1 -> registry-pg-2, RTO ~1.3-3s, recovery=recovered; hint 'registry-pg-1 re-seeded as a streaming standby of registry-pg-2 + its Redis re-pointed to the new master'; 5-instant timeline table.

The promoted node .118 returns 'f' (primary) and holds the VIP; ssh .117 returns 't' (streaming standby) with pg_stat_wal_receiver=streaming -> 1 primary + 1 standby, NO split-brain (was the gap: the old demote.sh left a second PG primary).

observe.where: ssh nexusadmin@<node> "redis-cli -a $(sudo cat /etc/nexus-registry-pg/redis-password) --no-auth-warning info replication | grep role"
observe.what: New primary Redis role:master; old primary role:slave -> Redis re-attached via notify_backup demote.sh.

observe.where: psql "host=192.168.70.118 dbname=registry user=harbor sslmode=require"  (harbor pw at KV nexus/registry/harbor-db-password)
observe.what: The harbor role is ADMITTED over TLS on the promoted node (pg_hba NEXUS-REGISTRY-HBA now on both nodes) -> Harbor's DB connection via the VIP survives the cutover. Pre-fix this was refused.

whatProves: RegistryAdapter.FailoverAsync --direction registry-db is a real self-healing one-shot datastore failover (was DR-deferred). It performs a keepalived VRRP cutover of the .119 datastore VIP (PG + Redis), promotes PG + re-masters Redis, then deterministically fences + pg_basebackup re-seeds the demoted old primary as a streaming standby (no split-brain) and re-points its Redis to the new master. The promoted node serves Harbor because the NEXUS-REGISTRY-HBA block now exists on BOTH nodes. Symmetric in both directions (re-run to fail back). Reuses the iceberg-pg (0.L.2.1) fence/re-seed pattern.
